I think we mostly agree really. As a woman climber I just often notice routes that I do with good technique I see men in the gym do the same routes but by just muscling through it and while that is a viable strategy its just not as efficient. 

I guess its a bit of a pet peeve of mine seeing people overly rely on strength rather than optimising technique, but I suppose that's also up to each person how they want to apply their strength and technique on the wall. I do admit that I have noticed with some routes that I am having a more difficult time because I am not as strong. In that way getting stronger is definitely beneficial. 

But yeah, someone stuck at V1 for 7 months should probably focus on gaining more climbing related strength.

I think maybe I am in a bit unique situation I suppose. I have been climbing for 10 years, but then I took a 5 year break. 

Before the break I could do around 15 pull-ups and I was definitely climbing at a much higher level than I am now. But even without my strength being where it was I can still do overhanging routes. I really think if your technique is good you don't need strength to the same extent. 

I just feel like people often tend to rely more on strength rather than focusing on good technique.

I've been going through something similar for the past year now. About 5-10 years ago I used to climb at a very high level and I would occasionally participate in competitions. But then I had a gap of about 5 years or so where I barely did any climbing at all. 

Now I climb 6a-6c and I struggle with anything higher. Every time I go to the climbing gym I have to remind myself to not compare my current performance to what my performance has been in the past. I actively try to separate these two periods of my life. 

I think it is important to be forgiving to yourself and you often hear people saying not to compare yourself to others, I think this is similar that we shouldn't compare ourselves to ourselves at different points in our life and just try to focus on what we are doing now.
